evidence.title: Seasonal pattern of latex spoilage (aggregate)
evidence.text: Pre-coagulation is the largest spoilage cause in every season. Its share of total spoilage is about 71% in June-August versus about 47% in December-February. Aggregates only; no estate or worker records.

evidence.title: Warehouse storage audit, Plant 3, April to June 2026
evidence.text: Warehouse storage audit, Plant 3, April to June 2026 Audit of 6 and 7 July 2026 by the raw material team of CEAT. All four bays of the raw material warehouse are covered and ventilated, and every bale of natural rubber stood on a pallet. 1,180 of the 1,229 issue lines followed first in, first out. 11 of the 412 lots in store were past the time-to-use limit of their grade.

evidence.title: Cause mix across the year (aggregate)
evidence.text: Contamination losses stay between 0.77% and 0.85% of latex collected in every month, so they are a steady, controllable cause. Temperature-related losses peak in March-May at about 1.1% of latex collected.

evidence.title: Plant storage note, Kochi bales
evidence.text: Natural rubber bales from the Kochi supplier are kept on pallets in the covered bay and issued first in, first out. A bale stored for more than ninety days is given an ageing check before it goes to mixing. Dirt content and volatile matter are trended per supplier lot, so drift shows before the material reaches the mixer. Supplier feedback with the lot data attached goes out every month.

evidence.title: Spoilage by collection-to-factory time band (aggregate)
evidence.text: Total spoilage averages 3.6% of latex collected where the collection-to-factory time is under 2.5 hours, against 5.3% where it exceeds 3.5 hours. Cells with fewer than three estates are suppressed.

evidence.title: Warehouse storage practices for natural rubber
evidence.text: Rubber is stored in covered, ventilated warehouses, off the floor, away from direct sun and heat sources, with grades kept apart and first-in-first-out issue. Long-stored lots get an extra ageing check before use.

evidence.title: SOP - Monsoon operating procedure
evidence.text: Rain guards are fitted before the season; on rain days rounds are shorter and more frequent, anticoagulant dosing is increased and transport is prioritised.

evidence.title: SOP - Anticoagulant dosing and field preservation
evidence.text: Anticoagulant is prepared in measured batches by trained staff, dosed at the collection point on schedule, recorded per round, and increased on rain days.

evidence.title: Field-failure RCA pattern - material-handling-linked defects
evidence.text: A recurring share of failure reports trace to material handling rather than process settings: 18% of the mock failure reports in qms.db. The common thread is lots used after long or uneven storage.

evidence.title: SOP - Latex collection and cup handling
evidence.text: Rounds start at first light; cups are emptied within the agreed window after tapping; latex is strained into rinsed, covered buckets kept in shade; collection time is logged at the collection point.

evidence.title: Incoming natural-rubber lot acceptance and trending
evidence.text: Incoming natural-rubber lots are accepted against a small set of quality parameters (dirt content, volatile matter, plasticity retention and Mooney viscosity) with limits agreed with suppliers. Results are trended per supplier and per lot, so drift is seen before the material reaches mixing. No formulations are included.

body.question: How do I ingest my own graph as JSON?

response.answer:
Open **Context graph**, choose **Ingest data**, then pick a .json file or paste the JSON into the text box and press **Ingest**.

The JSON needs these fields:
- "graph": the name of the graph
- "company": the company that owns the data
- "nodes": each with a "type" and a "name"
- "edges": each with a "type", "source" and "target"

**Download sample** gives a small invented example in this format. A file can be up to 8,000,000 bytes.

Some defaults apply when you leave fields out. A missing sensitivity is Restricted, and a missing sharing keeps the graph to your company and mesh admins. A missing "synthetic" means the data is treated as real, so no cloud model reads it. Only a mesh admin can set "synthetic": true. If you want every company to read the graph (for example a graph of **Others**), set "sharing": "group" and a sensitivity of Internal or Public.

If a node type, an edge end or another needed field is missing, nothing is kept and each place to fix is listed, counting from 0. On success you get the graph id. Query the graph with POST /api/v1/context-graphs/<id>/query and a signed-in person's token.

The central service keeps an ingested graph as written, not at your company's node.

input.question: What does a compounding engineer need to know about natural rubber storage?

records.title: Warehouse storage practices for natural rubber
records.text: Rubber is stored in covered, ventilated warehouses, off the floor, away from direct sun and heat sources, with grades kept apart and first-in-first-out issue. Long-stored lots get an extra ageing check before use.

records.title: Incoming natural-rubber lot acceptance and trending
records.text: Incoming natural-rubber lots are accepted against a small set of quality parameters (dirt content, volatile matter, plasticity retention and Mooney viscosity) with limits agreed with suppliers. Results are trended per supplier and per lot, so drift is seen before the material reaches mixing. No formulations are included.

records.title: Plant storage note, Kochi bales
records.text: Natural rubber bales from the Kochi supplier are kept on pallets in the covered bay and issued first in, first out. A bale stored for more than ninety days is given an ageing check before it goes to mixing. Dirt content and volatile matter are trended per supplier lot, so drift shows before the material reaches the mixer. Supplier feedback with the lot data attached goes out every month.

records.title: Warehouse storage audit, Plant 3, April to June 2026
records.text: Warehouse storage audit, Plant 3, April to June 2026 Audit of 6 and 7 July 2026 by the raw material team of CEAT. All four bays of the raw material warehouse are covered and ventilated, and every bale of natural rubber stood on a pallet. 1,180 of the 1,229 issue lines followed first in, first out. 11 of the 412 lots in store were past the time-to-use limit of their grade.

records.title: Time-to-use limits and lot traceability
records.text: Each lot is tagged with receipt date and storage location, a maximum time before use is set per grade, and every mixing batch can be traced back to its supplier lot.

also_found_records.title: Cause mix across the year (aggregate)
also_found_records.text: Contamination losses stay between 0.77% and 0.85% of latex collected in every month, so they are a steady, controllable cause. Temperature-related losses peak in March-May at about 1.1% of latex collected.
